passages.title: The Library Slip Found inside the Wrong Book
sentences: On Monday, Emi borrowed a science book from the school library.
At home, a yellow slip fell from the book.
The slip had Koji's name and Friday's date, but the title on it was a history book.
Emi first thought the library had put the wrong slip in her science book.
Then she noticed a small call number on the slip and compared it with the number on her book.
The numbers were different, so she took the slip to the library without writing on it.
The librarian checked the return cart and found Koji's history book there.
Its pocket was empty, so the librarian returned the yellow slip to that book.
Emi learned to use several clues to identify where a paper belongs.
passages.fullTranslation: 月曜日、恵美は学校の図書館で理科の本を借りました。家で開くと、本から黄色い貸出票が落ちました。貸出票には浩二の名前と金曜日の日付がありましたが、書かれていた題名は歴史の本でした。恵美は最初、図書館が理科の本に間違った貸出票を入れたのだと思いました。そこで貸出票の小さな請求番号に気づき、自分の本の番号と比べました。番号は違っていたので、何も書き込まず貸出票を図書館へ持って行きました。司書が返却用の台車を調べると、そこに浩二の歴史の本がありました。その本のポケットは空だったため、司書は黄色い貸出票をその本へ戻しました。恵美は、複数の手がかりで紙の正しい場所を確かめられると学びました。

slashRows.jp: そこで貸出票の小さな請求番号に気づき、自分の本の番号と比べました。

slashRows.en: The numbers were different, so she took the slip to the library without writing on it.
slashRows.jp: 番号は違っていたので、何も書き込まず貸出票を図書館へ持って行きました。

slashRows.en: The librarian checked the return cart and found Koji's history book there.
slashRows.jp: 司書が返却用の台車を調べると、そこに浩二の歴史の本がありました。

slashRows.en: Its pocket was empty, so the librarian returned the yellow slip to that book.
slashRows.jp: その本のポケットは空だったため、司書は黄色い貸出票をその本へ戻しました。

slashRows.en: Emi learned to use several clues to identify where a paper belongs.
slashRows.jp: 恵美は、複数の手がかりで紙の正しい場所を確かめられると学びました。

questions.prompt: 貸出票には、持ち主や本を確かめるためのどんな情報が書かれていましたか。三つ答えなさい。
questions.answer: 浩二の名前、金曜日の日付、歴史の本という題名。
questions.evidence: The slip had Koji's name and Friday's date, but the title on it was a history book.
questions.evidenceJp: 貸出票には浩二の名前と金曜日の日付がありましたが、書かれていた題名は歴史の本でした。
questions.reason: 貸出票に書かれた三つの情報をそのまま確認します。

questions.prompt: 恵美が貸出票を自分の理科の本のものだと決めつけなかったのはなぜですか。
questions.answer: 貸出票の請求番号と自分の本の番号が違っていたから。
evidence: Then she noticed a small call number on the slip and compared it with the number on her book.
The numbers were different, so she took the slip to the library without writing on it.
evidenceJp: そこで貸出票の小さな請求番号に気づき、自分の本の番号と比べました。
番号は違っていたので、何も書き込まず貸出票を図書館へ持って行きました。
questions.reason: 番号を比較した結果が、最初の考えを見直す直接の理由になっています。

questions.evidenceJp: 司書が返却用の台車を調べると、そこに浩二の歴史の本がありました。

questions.evidence: Its pocket was empty, so the librarian returned the yellow slip to that book.

questions.reason: 空のポケットを確認した直後の行動を答えます。

questions.prompt: 「恵美は貸出票の請求番号に気づき、【　】。」の【　】に入る内容を本文に合わせて答えなさい。

その本のポケットは空だったため、司書は黄色い貸出票をその本へ戻しました。

questionSetB.prompt: この話から分かる、落とし物や書類の持ち主を確かめるときに大切なことは何ですか。
questionSetB.answer: 一つの見た目だけで決めず、名前・日付・番号など複数の手がかりを確かめること。
evidence: The slip had Koji's name and Friday's date, but the title on it was a history book.
Then she noticed a small call number on the slip and compared it with the number on her book.
Emi learned to use several clues to identify where a paper belongs.

passages.title: The Seed Cups Watered by Two Groups
sentences: Class 1-A planted bean seeds in twelve paper cups by the classroom window.
The morning group watered them and marked Monday on the care sheet.
After lunch, the afternoon group saw dry soil on top and watered every cup again.
The next day, two cups had water standing at the bottom, and one seed had moved above the soil.
The sheet showed that both groups had watered the cups on Monday.
They kept caring for the plants, but they changed the job record.
From Tuesday, each student wrote a name and time after the job.
The second group checked the record and watered only when no earlier mark was there.
The class learned that shared work needs a clear record.
passages.fullTranslation: 一年A組は教室の窓辺で十二個の紙コップに豆の種を植えました。朝の班は水をやり、世話の表の月曜日に印を付けました。昼食後、午後の班は表面の土が乾いているのを見て、全部のコップにもう一度水をやりました。翌日、二つのコップの底に水がたまり、一つの種は土の上へ動いていました。表を見ると、月曜日に二つの班が水をやっていたと分かりました。植物の世話は続けましたが、作業の記録方法を変えました。火曜日からは、各生徒が作業後に名前と時刻を書くことにしました。二つ目の班は記録を確かめ、前の印がないときだけ水をやりました。クラスは、共同作業には明確な記録が必要だと学びました。

questions.prompt: 午後の班がもう一度すべてのコップに水をやったのは、何を見たからですか。
questions.answer: 土の表面が乾いているのを見たから。
questions.evidence: After lunch, the afternoon group saw dry soil on top and watered every cup again.

questions.prompt: クラスが水やりの記録方法を変えることにしたのはなぜですか。
questions.answer: 月曜日に朝と午後の両方の班が同じ水やりをしていたと分かったから。
evidence: The next day, two cups had water standing at the bottom, and one seed had moved above the soil.
The sheet showed that both groups had watered the cups on Monday.
They kept caring for the plants, but they changed the job record.

表を見ると、月曜日に二つの班が水をやっていたと分かりました。
植物の世話は続けましたが、作業の記録方法を変えました。
questions.reason: 翌日の状態と記録確認によって二重の水やりが判明したことが変更理由です。

questions.prompt: 火曜日から、水やりをした生徒は何を記録することにしましたか。

questionSetB.answer: 月曜日に印を付けた。

questionSetB.prompt: 新しい記録方法によって、同じ日に二度水をやる失敗が減ると考えられるのはなぜですか。
questionSetB.answer: 後の班が、先に水やりをした人の名前と時刻を確認できるから。

evidence: From Tuesday, each student wrote a name and time after the job.
The second group checked the record and watered only when no earlier mark was there.

passages.title: A Morning Meeting Moved for Floor Cleaning
sentences: The student council planned a short meeting in Room 2 before school on Wednesday.
On Tuesday afternoon, a notice said cleaners would clean the second-floor rooms early Wednesday.
A new council message moved the meeting to the library at the same time.
Kenta had written Room 2 in his notebook on Monday and almost followed that older plan.
Before leaving home, he checked the message time and saw that the library notice was newer.
He went directly to the library instead of checking Room 2 first.
All members arrived there before the meeting began, while cleaners worked upstairs.
Afterward, the council added the word 'CHANGED' to future room-change messages.
Kenta learned to follow the newest dated notice after a schedule change.
passages.fullTranslation: 生徒会は水曜日の登校前に二番教室で短い会議をする予定でした。火曜日の午後、水曜日の朝早く清掃員が二階の教室を清掃するという案内が出ました。新しい生徒会連絡は、同じ時刻のまま会議を図書館へ変更しました。健太は月曜日にノートへ二番教室と書いており、その古い予定に従いそうになりました。家を出る前に連絡の時刻を確認すると、図書館への変更の方が新しいと分かりました。健太は二番教室を先に見に行かず、直接図書館へ向かいました。全員が会議開始前に図書館へ集まり、その間二階では清掃が行われました。その後、生徒会は今後の場所変更の連絡に「変更」と目立つよう書くことにしました。健太は、予定変更後は最新の日付の連絡に従うと学びました。

sentences: After school, Rina found a blue water bottle under a bench near the gym.
Three classmates had similar bottles, so color did not show the owner.
A small music-note sticker was on the bottom, and the name area was unclear.
Rina remembered that the music club had practiced in the gym that afternoon.
She did not give the bottle to a classmate who simply said it looked like his.
She took it to the music room and asked whether anyone used the same sticker.
Mao showed the matching sticker on her music folder and described a scratch beside the cap.
The scratch matched, so Rina returned the bottle to Mao.
Rina learned that matching details are stronger clues than appearance alone.

passages.title: A Lunch Tray Count after the Class Trip Changed
sentences: The lunch staff prepared trays for thirty-two students in Class 1-C.
That morning, eight students left school for a half-day class trip before lunch.
The old lunch list still showed thirty-two students.
Yuna counted the class and found twenty-four students in the classroom.
She did not throw away the extra lunches or guess who needed them.
She told the teacher before lunch service and showed the new class count.
The teacher called the lunch room, which had not yet placed food on the extra trays.
The lunch room sent only twenty-four trays, and the extra trays stayed clean for another class.
Yuna learned to update quantities when the number of people changes.

passages.title: The Notebook Pages Mixed by an Open Window
sentences: Haruto left his project notebook open while carrying books.
A strong wind came through the window and blew three loose pages onto the floor.
The pages had no numbers, but the ending of each page gave a clue about what came next.
One page described planting seeds, another showed the first leaves, and a third recorded flowers.
Haruto did not put them back in the order in which he picked them up.
He read the dates and the changes in the plant from each page.
The seed page came first, the leaf page followed it, and the flower record came later.

passages.title: A Relay Order Changed after a Student Hurt a Foot
sentences: Four students practiced a relay for the school sports day.
Their usual order was Aki, Ren, Yuto, and Mei, and Yuto ran the long third section.
During Tuesday practice, Yuto hurt his foot, and the nurse said, “Do not run tomorrow.”
The team first thought about leaving his place empty, but a relay needed four runners.
They asked reserve runner Saki which section she had practiced.
Saki had practiced the second section, so Ren moved to Yuto's longer third section.
The new order became Aki, Saki, Ren, and Mei, and they practiced the two changed handoffs.
Yuto watched from the side and helped check their marks instead of running.
The team learned that a safe replacement also changes the surrounding order.

passages.title: The Flower Vase Moved away from the Heater
sentences: The class placed a vase of white flowers on a shelf for an open-school day.
By the next morning, the flowers nearest the classroom heater were bending down.
The water level was still high, so Nami looked at the space around the vase.
She felt warm dry air blowing from the heater onto the flowers.
Nami did not add more water because the vase was already nearly full.
With the teacher, she moved the vase to a bright table away from the hot air.
They marked both positions and compared the flowers again that afternoon.
The moved flowers were no longer bending as quickly, although the damaged flowers did not stand up again.
Nami learned to change a condition that matched the observed problem.

passages.title: The Old Entrance Still Shown on a School Map
sentences: A printed school map showed visitors entering through the east gate.
On Friday, Kota saw a new sign outside: “Visitors, use the south gate.”
Construction had closed the east gate, but several old maps were still beside the station.
Kota checked the date at the bottom of one map and saw a date from last year.
He kept the map because many roads were still correct.
He told the teacher, and they placed a bright correction sticker over the old entrance arrow.
The sticker directed visitors to the south gate until construction ended.
The school also put a new digital map online and marked the old printed copies clearly.
Kota learned that an old map sometimes needs one important current correction.

passages.title: An Eraser Returned inside the Wrong Pencil Case
sentences: Mika found a white eraser inside her pencil case after art class.
She already had her blue eraser, so the white one was not hers.
The white eraser had a small star cut into one corner and a faint letter K.
During art, four pencil cases were together on one table.
Mika did not decide from K alone because two students had K names.
She asked both students to describe the missing erasers before showing it.
Kei said his had a star cut made by his older sister, while Kumi said hers had a red cover.
Mika returned the eraser to Kei and checked her case for other mixed items.
She learned that asking for a detail first can confirm an owner fairly.

passages.title: The Weather Chart with One Blank Tuesday
sentences: The science class recorded the weather at eight every morning for two weeks.
They made a wall chart, and Tuesday of the second week was blank.
Monday was sunny and Wednesday cloudy, but neither proved Tuesday's weather.
Ryo checked the class notebook and found that the student on duty had been absent Tuesday.
The class did not fill the blank by copying a nearby day.
They looked for another school record from the same time.
The garden club had written 'light rain at 8:00' on its watering sheet that Tuesday.
The class added light rain to the chart and wrote 'garden club record' below the entry.
Ryo learned to fill a missing record with evidence, not a nearby-day guess.
passages.fullTranslation: 理科のクラスは二週間、毎朝八時に天気を記録しました。壁の表を作ると、二週目の火曜日だけ空白でした。月曜は晴れ、水曜は曇りでしたが、どちらも火曜の天気を証明しませんでした。亮がクラスノートを調べると、火曜日の係の生徒が欠席していたと分かりました。クラスは前後の日を写して空欄を埋めませんでした。同じ時刻の別の学校記録がないか調べました。園芸部はその火曜日の水やり表に「8時、小雨」と書いていました。クラスは表に小雨と加え、その下に「園芸部記録」と書きました。亮は、欠けた記録は前後の日の推測でなく証拠で補うと学びました。

slashRows.en: The science class recorded the weather at eight every morning for two weeks.
slashRows.jp: 理科のクラスは二週間、毎朝八時に天気を記録しました。

slashRows.en: They made a wall chart, and Tuesday of the second week was blank.
slashRows.jp: 壁の表を作ると、二週目の火曜日だけ空白でした。

slashRows.en: Monday was sunny and Wednesday cloudy, but neither proved Tuesday's weather.
slashRows.jp: 月曜は晴れ、水曜は曇りでしたが、どちらも火曜の天気を証明しませんでした。

slashRows.en: Ryo checked the class notebook and found that the student on duty had been absent Tuesday.
slashRows.jp: 亮がクラスノートを調べると、火曜日の係の生徒が欠席していたと分かりました。

slashRows.en: The class did not fill the blank by copying a nearby day.
slashRows.jp: クラスは前後の日を写して空欄を埋めませんでした。

slashRows.en: They looked for another school record from the same time.
slashRows.jp: 同じ時刻の別の学校記録がないか調べました。

slashRows.en: The garden club had written 'light rain at 8:00' on its watering sheet that Tuesday.
slashRows.jp: 園芸部はその火曜日の水やり表に「8時、小雨」と書いていました。

slashRows.en: The class added light rain to the chart and wrote 'garden club record' below the entry.
slashRows.jp: クラスは表に小雨と加え、その下に「園芸部記録」と書きました。

slashRows.en: Ryo learned to fill a missing record with evidence, not a nearby-day guess.
slashRows.jp: 亮は、欠けた記録は前後の日の推測でなく証拠で補うと学びました。

passages.title: The Classroom Plant Leaning toward the Window
sentences: A small classroom plant stood on a shelf near the back wall.
After one week, its top leaves leaned strongly toward the window on the left.
Mina wondered whether the plant was simply falling because one side was heavier.
She checked the pot and found it stable, while the new stems were bending toward the light.
She did not cut the leaning stems or tie them straight immediately.
The class turned the pot halfway around and marked its new position.
Three days later, the newest leaves had begun turning back toward the window.
They continued turning the pot a little each week so different sides received light.
Mina learned that changing one condition and observing later can test an idea without damaging the plant.
passages.fullTranslation: 小さな教室の植物が後ろの壁近くの棚に置かれていました。一週間後、上の葉が左側の窓へ大きく傾いていました。美奈は、片側が重くて倒れかけているだけではないかと思いました。鉢は安定しており、新しい茎が光の方向へ曲がっていることを確認しました。傾いた茎をすぐ切ったり、まっすぐ縛ったりはしませんでした。クラスは鉢を半回転させ、新しい向きを記録しました。三日後、最も新しい葉は再び窓の方へ向き始めました。さまざまな側が光を受けるよう、毎週少しずつ鉢を回すことにしました。美奈は、一つの条件を変えて後で観察すれば植物を傷つけず考えを確かめられると学びました。

passages.title: A Club Badge Box with Two Different Sizes
sentences: The tennis club received a box of new cloth badges for its uniforms.
The box held small and large badges together.
The order sheet showed eight small and twelve large badges for twenty members.
Yuki first planned to hand them out from the box, risking wrong sizes.
She checked the uniform list, which already recorded each member's badge size.
The club separated the badges into two trays and labeled them S and L.
They counted eight in the S tray and twelve in the L tray before distribution.
The members said their names one by one, and Yuki matched each name with the size on the list.
The club learned that sorting by recorded size prevents mix-ups.
passages.fullTranslation: テニス部はユニフォーム用の新しい布バッジが入った箱を受け取りました。箱には小さいバッジと大きいバッジが一緒に入っていました。注文表には二十人分として小八枚、大十二枚とありました。由紀は最初箱からそのまま配ろうとし、サイズ違いの恐れがありました。そこで、各部員のバッジサイズが記録されているユニフォーム表を確認しました。部はバッジを二つのトレーに分け、SとLの表示を付けました。配る前にSが八枚、Lが十二枚あることを数えました。部員たちは順番に名前を言い、由紀がそれぞれの名前を表のサイズと照合しました。部は、記録されたサイズで先に分けると取り違えを防げると学びました。

passages.title: The Two Gloves That Did Not Make a Pair
sentences: After a cold morning, the lost-item box held two black gloves.
They looked similar from far away, so Taku put them together as one pair.
He picked them up and saw that both were left-hand gloves.
One had three gray lines at the wrist, while the other had a small red thread near the thumb.
Taku did not pair them just because their color matched.
He placed each glove separately and added a note about the place.
Later, one student described the gray lines and another described the red thread.
Each student received one glove and continued looking for its true partner.
Taku learned to check side and details before pairing similar lost items.

passages.title: A Hallway Display Put Up One Day Too Early
sentences: The art club prepared a hallway display for a Friday school event.
On Wednesday, a student read the calendar quickly and thought the event was Thursday.
The club put all the pictures on the hallway wall that afternoon.
A teacher then pointed out that another class needed the wall for a Thursday morning presentation.
The club checked the event calendar and confirmed Friday as its display date.
They did not ask the other class to change its scheduled presentation.
They removed the pictures, numbered their order, and stored them overnight.
After the Thursday presentation ended, the club used the numbered sheet to rebuild the display for Friday.
The students learned to check the date and shared-space schedule first.
passages.fullTranslation: 美術部は金曜日の学校行事に向けて廊下の展示を準備しました。水曜日、一人の生徒がカレンダーを急いで見て行事は木曜日だと思いました。部はその日の午後、すべての絵を廊下の壁に飾りました。先生が、その壁は木曜朝に別のクラスが発表で使うと伝えました。部が行事予定を確認すると、自分たちの展示日は金曜日だと確認できました。別のクラスに予定された発表を変えてもらうことはしませんでした。絵を外し、順番に番号を付けて一晩保管しました。木曜の発表後、番号表を使って金曜日の展示を作り直しました。生徒たちは、先に日付と共有場所の予定を確認すると学びました。

passages.title: The Aquarium Feeding Mark Written in the Wrong Row
sentences: Two students took turns feeding the fish in the classroom aquarium.
On Thursday morning, Sota saw no mark in the Thursday row of the feeding chart.
He was about to feed the fish, but a fresh mark in Friday's row stopped him.
Friday had not come yet, so Sota asked Aya about the mark in the wrong row.
Aya remembered feeding the fish ten minutes earlier and confirmed the mistake.
Sota did not feed the fish a second time.
They moved the mark to Thursday and added the feeding time beside it.
From then on, the feeder said the day aloud before making a mark.
Sota learned that an impossible date can be a clue to check a record before repeating a care task.
passages.fullTranslation: 二人の生徒が交代で教室の水槽の魚に餌をやっていました。木曜の朝、颯太は餌やり表の木曜日の欄に印がないのを見ました。魚に餌をやろうとしましたが、金曜日の欄の新しい印を見て手を止めました。金曜日はまだなので、颯太は彩に間違った欄の印について尋ねました。彩は10分前に餌をやったことを思い出し、記入ミスを確認しました。颯太は魚に二回目の餌をやりませんでした。印を木曜日へ移し、その横に餌をやった時刻も書きました。それ以降、餌をやる人は印を付ける前に曜日を声に出すことにしました。颯太は、あり得ない日付は世話を重ねる前に記録を確認する手がかりになると学びました。

passages.title: A Choir Folder Taken to the Practice Room Next Door
sentences: The school choir practiced in Music Room A after lunch.
Practice ended, but Miki did not find the blue folder with the alto music.
Someone remembered moving two folders into Music Room B next door.
Miki checked Room B but first saw only a similar blue folder for the brass band.
She left it because its label clearly said 'Brass.'
She looked beside the piano bench and found another blue folder partly under a black case.
Its label said 'Choir Alto,' and the first page matched the song they had practiced.
Miki returned it to the choir shelf and wrote Room B on the temporary move note.
She learned to trace a moved object and check its label before taking it.

passages.title: The Cafeteria Portion Test after Too Much Rice Was Left
sentences: The cafeteria team noticed that many bowls still held rice after lunch on three Mondays.
At first, they thought students simply disliked Monday's main dishes.
They weighed the leftover rice and found much more waste than on Tuesday or Wednesday.
A short survey showed that most students liked the food but felt the standard rice serving was too large.
The team did not reduce every meal immediately; one week's result did not show all students.
For two weeks, one line offered a slightly smaller first serving and allowed students to ask for more.
Waste fell, while the number of students asking for a second serving stayed small.
The cafeteria then kept the smaller first portion but continued recording waste each week.
They learned that reducing food waste works better when a change is tested and students can still request enough food.
passages.fullTranslation: 給食係は三週続けて月曜日の昼食後、多くの茶わんにご飯が残っていることに気づきました。最初は、月曜日の主菜が生徒に好まれていないのだと思いました。残ったご飯を量ると、火曜や水曜よりかなり多いと分かりました。短いアンケートでは、多くの生徒が料理は好きだが標準のご飯量が多すぎると答えました。一週間の結果だけでは全員の様子を示せないため、すぐすべての食事量を減らしませんでした。二週間、一つの列では最初の量を少し減らし、必要ならおかわりできるようにしました。残飯は減り、おかわりを求める生徒数も少ないままでした。そこで給食係は最初の量を少なめにしつつ、毎週残飯量を記録し続けました。生徒たちは、食品ロス削減は変更を試しつつ必要量を追加できるようにするとよりよく進むと学びました。

passages.title: Rainwater Collected beside the Bicycle Parking Area
sentences: After heavy rain, students found a wide puddle beside the bicycle parking area.
Riders had to step into the water when they moved bicycles from the back row.
The environment club first suggested adding more gravel everywhere around the parking area.
Before buying anything, they watched the next rain and saw water flowing from one roof pipe toward a low corner.
They realized that covering the whole area would cost more without changing where most water arrived.
With the school manager, they cleared leaves from a nearby drain and made a shallow gravel channel from the pipe to it.
During the next storm, the channel carried most water away and the puddle became much smaller.
The club marked the remaining wet spot for another check rather than claiming the problem was completely solved.
They learned that observing how water actually moves can lead to a smaller and more useful repair.
passages.fullTranslation: 大雨の後、生徒たちは自転車置き場の横に大きな水たまりを見つけました。奥の列から自転車を出すとき、利用者は水の中へ足を入れなければなりませんでした。環境部は最初、自転車置き場の周り全体に砂利を増やす案を出しました。購入前に次の雨を観察すると、一本の雨どいから低い角へ水が流れていると分かりました。全体を覆っても、多くの水が来る場所は変わらず費用だけ増えると気づきました。学校管理者と一緒に近くの排水口の葉を取り、雨どいからそこへ浅い砂利の水路を作りました。次の嵐では水路が大部分の水を流し、水たまりはかなり小さくなりました。部は問題が完全に解決したとせず、残った湿った場所を次の確認用に記録しました。生徒たちは、水が実際にどう動くか観察すれば、より小さく効果的な改善につながると学びました。

passages.title: The Stream Litter Count Made after a Strong Storm
sentences: A class counted litter beside a local stream once each month.
In June they found twenty-two pieces, but in July they counted sixty-eight.
Some students said people started dropping much more trash in July.
The teacher reminded them that a strong storm had flooded the stream two days before the July count.
The class realized that storm water possibly carried litter from other places into their study area.
They kept the July number but labeled it 'after major storm' instead of removing it.
One week later, they made an extra count under normal water conditions and found thirty-one pieces.
Their report showed all three numbers and explained why the July result should not be treated as a normal month alone.
The class learned that unusual conditions should be recorded because they can change what a comparison means.
passages.fullTranslation: クラスは毎月一度、地域の小川のごみを数えていました。六月は二十二個でしたが、七月には六十八個数えました。何人かの生徒は、七月に人々が急に多くごみを捨て始めたと言いました。先生は、七月の調査二日前に強い嵐で小川が増水したことを思い出させました。クラスは、嵐の水が別の場所から調査区域へごみを運んだ可能性があると気づきました。七月の数字は削除せず、「大きな嵐の後」と注記しました。一週間後、通常の水量で追加調査すると三十一個でした。報告書には三つの数字を示し、七月だけを通常月として扱えない理由を説明しました。クラスは、異常な条件は比較の意味を変えるため記録すべきだと学びました。

passages.title: A Garden Watering Plan during a Hot Week
sentences: The gardening club cared for vegetables during a week of unusually hot weather.
Its normal plan watered every bed lightly at four in the afternoon.
By Wednesday, leaves in the sunniest bed were drooping before lunch even though the soil had been watered the day before.
The club had a limited water supply and could not simply double the amount for every bed.
They checked the soil early in the morning and found that shaded beds were still damp while the sunny bed was dry.
They changed the plan so the sunny bed received more water early in the morning, when less water would evaporate quickly.
The shaded beds kept their smaller amount and were checked before any extra watering.
By Friday, the sunny plants were less wilted and the club had stayed within its weekly water limit.
The club learned to match a hot-weather plan to each bed.
passages.fullTranslation: 園芸部は非常に暑い一週間、野菜の世話をしました。通常は午後四時にすべての畑へ少量ずつ水をやっていました。水をやった翌日でも、水曜には最も日当たりのよい畑の葉が昼前にしおれていました。使える水に限りがあり、すべての畑の量を単純に二倍にはできませんでした。朝早く土を調べると、日陰の畑はまだ湿っていましたが日なたは乾いていました。日なたの畑には蒸発しにくい朝早くに多めの水をやるよう変更しました。日陰の畑は少なめの量を続け、追加前に土を確認しました。金曜までに日なたの植物はしおれにくくなり、週の水使用量も上限内でした。園芸部は、暑い時期の計画を各畑の条件に合わせると学びました。

slashRows.jp: 日なたの畑には蒸発しにくい朝早くに多めの水をやるよう変更しました。

passages.title: The Library Shelf Display That Changed What Students Borrowed
sentences: The library placed six nature books on a bright display near the entrance for one month.
Those books were borrowed much more often than they had been during the previous month.
A student wrote that the display proved everyone had suddenly become more interested in nature.
The librarian pointed out that the books had also become easier to see and reach.
The committee realized that borrowing numbers alone could not show whether interest or visibility caused the change.
The next month, they displayed six history books in the same place and recorded their borrowing too.
History borrowing also rose, although not by exactly the same amount.
The final report said displays appeared to influence borrowing but did not claim they changed students' long-term interests.
The committee learned to separate what a pattern suggests from what the available evidence can actually prove.
passages.fullTranslation: 図書館は一か月、入口近くの目立つ展示に自然の本六冊を置きました。その本は前月よりずっと多く借りられました。ある生徒は、みんなが急に自然へ関心を持った証拠だと書きました。司書は、本が以前より見つけやすく手に取りやすくなったことも指摘しました。委員会は、貸出数だけでは興味と見やすさのどちらが変化の原因か分からないと気づきました。翌月、同じ場所に歴史の本六冊を展示し、貸出数を記録しました。歴史の本の貸出も増えましたが、増え方は同じではありませんでした。最終報告は展示が貸出に影響するようだと述べましたが、長期的な興味まで変えたとは主張しませんでした。委員会は、傾向が示すことと証拠で実際に証明できることを分けると学びました。

passages.title: A Limited Repair Budget for Sports Equipment
sentences: The sports committee had money for repairs to only three of five damaged items.
The list included two volleyball nets, a ball cart, a bench, and a scoreboard stand.
At first, students wanted to repair three items with high club use.
The PE teacher said they also needed a record of safety risk and frequency of use.
One bench had a sharp broken edge, while one net was old but could still be used safely for practice.
The committee ranked each item by safety, whether another item could replace it, and repair cost.
They repaired the bench, the unstable scoreboard stand, and the ball cart first.
They marked the damaged nets for limited use and requested money for them in the next budget.
The committee learned that limited money should be used first where delay creates the greatest practical risk.

passages.title: The Animal Shelter Visit with Three Volunteer Jobs
sentences: A class planned to volunteer for two hours at a local animal shelter.
The shelter offered three jobs: washing bowls, preparing food, and walking calm adult dogs.
Several students immediately chose dog walking because it sounded the most enjoyable.
The staff explained that walkers needed a full hour, closed shoes, and confidence holding a lead.
Two students had to leave early for a bus, and one student was uncomfortable around large dogs.
The class matched jobs to available time and comfort instead of treating one task as the best volunteer work.
Students leaving early washed bowls, the student uneasy with dogs prepared food, and trained groups walked the dogs.
All three jobs were finished before the visit ended, and nobody had to take a role that felt unsafe.
The class learned that useful volunteering depends on what an organization needs and what each person can safely do.
passages.fullTranslation: クラスは地域の動物保護施設で二時間ボランティアをする計画を立てました。施設には食器洗い、餌の準備、おとなしい成犬の散歩という三つの仕事がありました。何人かの生徒は一番楽しそうだという理由ですぐ犬の散歩を選びました。職員は、散歩担当には一時間、つま先の閉じた靴、リードを持つ自信が必要だと説明しました。二人はバスのため早く帰る必要があり、一人は大きな犬が苦手でした。クラスは一つの仕事を最良とせず、使える時間と得意不得意に仕事を合わせました。早く帰る生徒は食器洗い、犬が苦手な生徒は餌準備、説明を受けた班は散歩を担当しました。訪問終了までに三つの仕事が終わり、危険に感じる役割を無理にする人はいませんでした。クラスは、役立つボランティアは施設の必要と各人が安全にできることの両方で決まると学びました。

passages.title: A Winter Walking Route That Became Dark before Club Ended
sentences: In September, the basketball club walked from school to a nearby station after practice.
The usual route passed a riverside path that was quiet and pleasant in daylight.
By November, practice still ended at five thirty, but the riverside path was already dark.
One student nearly missed a low step; only a few lights were near that section.
The club realized that a route safe in early autumn was not automatically safe under winter light conditions.
They compared a slightly longer main-road route that had sidewalks, shops, and streetlights.
For winter practices, the team used the main road and asked students not to walk alone after the group separated.
They planned to review the riverside route again when practice ended in daylight in spring.
The club learned that route safety can change with season and time even when the road itself has not changed.

passages.title: The Recycled Paper Notebook That Tore at the Binding
sentences: An environment club tested notebooks made from recycled paper for next year's school store.
The paper wrote smoothly, and students liked the simple cover design.
After two weeks, however, several pages began tearing close to the metal binding.
At first, the club thought the recycled paper itself was too weak.
They compared unused sheets and found that the paper away from the holes did not tear easily.
The holes had been punched very close to the edge, leaving only a narrow strip of paper around the binding.
The maker produced a small trial with the holes moved farther inward and a slightly wider inner margin.
After another two-week test, the same paper stayed attached much better.
The club learned to locate the failure point before blaming an entire material for a product problem.
passages.fullTranslation: 環境部は翌年の学校売店用に再生紙ノートを試しました。紙は書きやすく、生徒たちは簡単な表紙デザインも気に入りました。しかし二週間後、何枚かのページが金属のとじ部分近くで破れ始めました。最初、部は再生紙そのものが弱すぎると思いました。未使用の紙と比べると、穴から離れた部分は簡単には破れませんでした。穴が端に近すぎ、金属の周りに細い紙しか残っていませんでした。製造者は穴を少し内側へ移し、内側余白を広くした試作品を作りました。もう二週間試すと、同じ紙でもかなり外れにくくなりました。環境部は、製品の問題を素材全体のせいにする前に壊れた場所を特定すべきだと学びました。

passages.title: A Music Rehearsal Changed after the Sound Echoed from the Wall
sentences: The school band moved its rehearsal to a wide hall while the music room was repaired.
Players near the back wall heard repeated sounds and had trouble following the conductor's beat.
The band first played more loudly, but the echo became stronger instead of clearer.
The teacher asked groups to stop and listen from different positions in the hall.
They found that the strongest echo occurred where brass instruments faced the hard back wall directly.
The band turned the brass section slightly inward and moved two rows farther from the wall.
They also placed thick stage curtains behind the section where possible.
A second rehearsal sounded clearer, and players could follow the beat without increasing volume.
The band learned that changing position and surfaces can solve an acoustic problem, while louder playing can worsen the problem.
passages.fullTranslation: 音楽室の修理中、吹奏楽部は広いホールへ練習場所を移しました。後ろの壁近くの演奏者は音が反響し、指揮の拍を追いにくく感じました。最初はより大きな音で演奏しましたが、明瞭になるどころか反響が強くなりました。先生は演奏を止め、ホールの別々の位置で音を聞くよう求めました。金管楽器が硬い後ろ壁へ直接向く場所で反響が最も強いと分かりました。金管楽器を少し内側へ向け、二列を壁から離しました。可能な場所にはその後ろへ厚い舞台カーテンも置きました。二回目の練習では音が明瞭になり、音量を上げずに拍を追えました。楽団は、位置や周囲の面を変えることで音響の問題を改善でき、大きく演奏するだけではその問題を悪化させることもあると学びました。

passages.title: The Curtain Trial for a Classroom That Became Too Warm
sentences: A south-facing classroom became very warm during sunny afternoons in early summer.
Students suggested keeping all curtains closed from morning until school ended.
The teacher said, “Compare temperature and light before making a permanent rule.”
For three days, they closed the sunniest windows after lunch and left the other curtains open.
The afternoon temperature fell a little, and students could still read without turning on every light.
On a cloudy day, closing the same curtains made the room darker but did not reduce heat in a useful way.
The class changed its plan to use the curtains only when direct sun reached the desks.
They kept ventilation and the school's heat-safety rules as separate requirements.
The students learned that a simple shade measure can help under the right condition without becoming an all-day rule.
passages.fullTranslation: 南向きの教室は初夏の晴れた午後、とても暑くなりました。生徒たちは朝から下校までカーテンを全部閉める案を出しました。先生は「恒久的な決まりを作る前に、温度と光を比べてください」と言いました。三日間、昼食後に最も日が当たる窓だけカーテンを閉め、ほかは開けました。午後の温度は少し下がり、すべての照明を点けなくても読書できました。曇りの日に同じカーテンを閉めると、部屋は暗くなりましたが有効な温度低下はありませんでした。クラスは、直射日光が机へ届くときだけカーテンを使うことにしました。換気と学校の暑さ対策規則は別の必要条件として続けました。生徒たちは、簡単な日よけも適切な条件では役立つが一日中の規則にする必要はないと学びました。

slashRows.en: The afternoon temperature fell a little, and students could still read without turning on every light.
slashRows.jp: 午後の温度は少し下がり、すべての照明を点けなくても読書できました。

slashRows.en: On a cloudy day, closing the same curtains made the room darker but did not reduce heat in a useful way.
slashRows.jp: 曇りの日に同じカーテンを閉めると、部屋は暗くなりましたが有効な温度低下はありませんでした。

slashRows.en: The class changed its plan to use the curtains only when direct sun reached the desks.
slashRows.jp: クラスは、直射日光が机へ届くときだけカーテンを使うことにしました。

slashRows.en: They kept ventilation and the school's heat-safety rules as separate requirements.
slashRows.jp: 換気と学校の暑さ対策規則は別の必要条件として続けました。

passages.title: A Charity Sale with Too Many Unsold Small Items
sentences: A class held a charity sale with handmade bookmarks, cards, and small cloth bags.
At the end of the first day, most bags had sold, but many bookmarks and cards remained.
Some students wanted to cut every price in half the next morning.
The sales record showed that the bags were already selling well at their original price.
The class realized that lowering every price would reduce income without addressing which items were actually unsold.
They made a small set combining one bookmark and one card at a modest discount.
They kept the bag price unchanged and moved the sets beside the payment table where visitors could see them.
More small items sold on the second day, while the popular bags still brought in their full price.
The class learned that a sales change should respond to the specific pattern instead of changing successful items too.
passages.fullTranslation: クラスは手作りのしおり、カード、小さな布袋で慈善販売を行いました。初日終了時、袋はほとんど売れましたが、しおりとカードは多く残りました。何人かは翌朝すべての値段を半額にしようとしました。販売記録では、袋は元の値段ですでによく売れていました。全商品を値下げすると、実際に売れていない商品を区別せず収入を減らすと気づきました。しおり一枚とカード一枚を少し割引した小さなセットを作りました。袋の値段は変えず、セットを来客が見やすい会計台の横へ移しました。二日目は小物がより多く売れ、人気の袋は定価の収入を保ちました。クラスは、販売方法の変更はうまくいっている商品まで変えず、具体的な売れ方に対応すべきだと学びました。

passages.title: The Lost-Item Corner Reorganized by Where Things Were Found
sentences: The school lost-item corner held umbrellas, pencil cases, towels, keys, and many small objects.
Items were first grouped only by object type, but students still had trouble finding their own things.
Two black pencil cases looked almost identical, although one had been found in the gym and the other in the library.
The student council noticed that the discovery place was written in a notebook but not shown beside the objects.
They did not abandon categories because umbrellas and keys still needed different storage.
Instead, every item received a small tag with the date and place where it had been found.
Within each category, recent items were placed in front and older ones behind.
Students could now combine appearance with date and location when identifying property.
The council learned that organization works better when labels include the clues people actually use to recognize an item.

passages.title: A Community Book Box That Let Rain Reach the Bottom Shelf
sentences: Residents built a small outdoor book box where neighbors could exchange books.
After the first strong rain, books on the bottom shelf became damp while the upper books stayed dry.
The roof looked fine, so volunteers first considered replacing the whole box with a more expensive model.
During the next shower, one person watched and saw water running down the front door and under its lower edge.
They realized that the leak came from one opening rather than from every wall.
They added a narrow weather strip to the door and raised the bottom shelf several centimeters above the floor.
A tray outside also caught water dripping from umbrellas when people opened the box.
After two later storms, the bottom books remained dry, although volunteers continued checking the seal.
They learned to trace where damage begins before replacing an entire useful structure.
passages.fullTranslation: 住民は近所で本を交換できる小さな屋外本箱を作りました。最初の強い雨の後、上の本は乾いていましたが下段の本が湿りました。屋根は問題なさそうでしたが、ボランティアは最初箱全体を高価な物へ替えることを考えました。次の雨で観察すると、水が前扉を流れ、下の端から内側へ入るのが見えました。雨漏りは箱全体ではなく一つの隙間から来ていると分かりました。扉に細い防水材を付け、下段を床から数センチ高くしました。外には、本箱を開ける人の傘から落ちる水を受けるトレーも置きました。その後二回の嵐でも下段の本は乾いたままでしたが、ボランティアは防水部分の確認を続けました。住民は、役立つ物全体を交換する前に損傷が始まる場所を追うことが大切だと学びました。

passages.title: The School Garden Labels Faded before Harvest Time
sentences: The school garden used handwritten labels to show the names and planting dates of vegetables.
By midsummer, sunlight and rain had faded several labels until students could barely read them.
One group suggested writing the same words again with a darker pen.
Before doing that, they tested three marker types on spare plastic pieces outside for two weeks.
The darkest indoor marker faded quickly, while an outdoor paint marker remained clear after rain and sun.
The class copied the original plant names and dates from its garden notebook onto new labels.
They did not guess any missing date; one uncertain label was marked for the teacher to check.
The new labels stayed readable through harvest, and the test pieces were kept for next year's comparison.
The students learned that outdoor information needs materials tested under the weather it will actually face.
passages.fullTranslation: 学校菜園では手書きの札で野菜名と植え付け日を示していました。真夏までに日光と雨で何枚かの札が薄れ、生徒はほとんど読めなくなりました。ある班は同じ言葉をより濃いペンで書き直す案を出しました。その前に、三種類のペンを予備のプラスチック片へ書き、二週間外で試しました。最も濃い室内用ペンはすぐ薄れましたが、屋外用ペイントペンは雨と日光の後もはっきりしていました。クラスは菜園ノートから元の植物名と日付を新しい札へ写しました。分からない日付は推測せず、一枚は先生確認用の印を付けました。新しい札は収穫まで読める状態を保ち、試験片は翌年の比較用に残しました。生徒たちは、屋外情報には実際に受ける天候で試した材料が必要だと学びました。

passages.title: A Practice Match Stopped because the Water Bottles Ran Out
sentences: A soccer team brought one large box of water bottles to a two-hour practice match.
The coach had counted one bottle for each player and several extra for teachers.
The day became warmer than expected, and many players finished their first bottles before the second half.
Only four unopened bottles remained, which was not enough for both teams to continue safely.
The coaches stopped the match instead of asking players to wait until the end to drink.
They used a nearby indoor tap to refill personal bottles and extended the break.
For the next match, the team estimated water by time and weather, not only by the number of people.
They also identified the refill point before play began and assigned one adult to check supplies at each break.
The team learned that shared safety supplies need a backup plan when conditions can increase how much people use.
passages.fullTranslation: サッカーチームは二時間の練習試合に大きな箱一つ分の水を持って行きました。コーチは選手一人一本と先生用の予備数本を数えていました。予想より暑くなり、多くの選手が後半前に一本目を飲み終えました。未開封は四本だけで、両チームが安全に続けるには足りませんでした。コーチは試合終了まで水を我慢させず、試合を止めました。近くの屋内水道で各自のボトルへ水を補給し、休憩を延ばしました。次の試合では人数だけでなく時間と天候から必要な水を見積もりました。試合前に補給場所を確認し、各休憩で大人一人が残量を見ることにしました。チームは、条件によって必要量が増える共有の安全用品には予備計画が必要だと学びました。

slashRows.en: Only four unopened bottles remained, which was not enough for both teams to continue safely.

slashRows.en: The coaches stopped the match instead of asking players to wait until the end to drink.
slashRows.jp: コーチは試合終了まで水を我慢させず、試合を止めました。

slashRows.en: They used a nearby indoor tap to refill personal bottles and extended the break.
slashRows.jp: 近くの屋内水道で各自のボトルへ水を補給し、休憩を延ばしました。

slashRows.en: For the next match, the team estimated water by time and weather, not only by the number of people.
slashRows.jp: 次の試合では人数だけでなく時間と天候から必要な水を見積もりました。

slashRows.en: They also identified the refill point before play began and assigned one adult to check supplies at each break.
slashRows.jp: 試合前に補給場所を確認し、各休憩で大人一人が残量を見ることにしました。

slashRows.en: The team learned that shared safety supplies need a backup plan when conditions can increase how much people use.
slashRows.jp: チームは、条件によって必要量が増える共有の安全用品には予備計画が必要だと学びました。

passages.title: The River Temperature Log and the Fish Seen near One Bridge
sentences: A science class measured river temperature at the same bridge every Friday for six weeks.
They also wrote down which fish they could see from the bank during a ten-minute observation.
In the first four weeks, water stayed near eighteen degrees and students usually saw several small fish.
During a hot fifth week, the temperature reached twenty-three degrees and they saw only one fish.
Some students wanted to conclude that warmer water had driven all the fish away.
The teacher asked what their observation could actually tell them about the whole river.
The class had watched only one bridge, at one time of day, and only from the surface.
On the sixth week, water was still warm, but eight fish appeared near shaded stones below the bridge.
Students added shade and observation position to their log instead of recording temperature alone.
Their report said fish sightings changed during the study but did not claim temperature was the only cause.
They suggested measuring at another bridge and at different times before making a stronger ecological conclusion.
The class learned that a limited observation can reveal a pattern without proving what happens everywhere.
passages.fullTranslation: 理科のクラスは六週間、毎週金曜日に同じ橋で川の水温を測りました。さらに岸から十分間観察し、見えた魚を記録しました。最初の四週間は水温が十八度前後で、小さな魚を何匹か見られました。暑い第五週には二十三度まで上がり、魚は一匹しか見えませんでした。一部の生徒は、水温上昇ですべての魚が逃げたと結論づけようとしました。先生は、その観察から川全体について何が本当に言えるか尋ねました。クラスは一つの橋で一日の一時刻、しかも水面からだけ観察していました。第六週も水は暖かいままでしたが、橋の下の日陰の石近くに八匹の魚が現れました。生徒たちは水温だけでなく、日陰と観察位置も記録に加えました。報告は調査中に魚の目撃数が変わったと述べましたが、水温だけが原因とはしませんでした。より強い生態的結論を出す前に、別の橋や異なる時刻でも測ることを提案しました。クラスは、限られた観察でも傾向は見えるが、どこでも同じだと証明するわけではないと学びました。

slashRows.jp: 理科のクラスは六週間、毎週金曜日に同じ橋で川の水温を測りました。

slashRows.en: They also wrote down which fish they could see from the bank during a ten-minute observation.
slashRows.jp: さらに岸から十分間観察し、見えた魚を記録しました。

slashRows.en: In the first four weeks, water stayed near eighteen degrees and students usually saw several small fish.
slashRows.jp: 最初の四週間は水温が十八度前後で、小さな魚を何匹か見られました。

slashRows.en: During a hot fifth week, the temperature reached twenty-three degrees and they saw only one fish.
slashRows.jp: 暑い第五週には二十三度まで上がり、魚は一匹しか見えませんでした。

slashRows.en: Some students wanted to conclude that warmer water had driven all the fish away.
slashRows.jp: 一部の生徒は、水温上昇ですべての魚が逃げたと結論づけようとしました。

slashRows.en: The teacher asked what their observation could actually tell them about the whole river.
slashRows.jp: 先生は、その観察から川全体について何が本当に言えるか尋ねました。

slashRows.en: The class had watched only one bridge, at one time of day, and only from the surface.
slashRows.jp: クラスは一つの橋で一日の一時刻、しかも水面からだけ観察していました。

slashRows.en: On the sixth week, water was still warm, but eight fish appeared near shaded stones below the bridge.
slashRows.jp: 第六週も水は暖かいままでしたが、橋の下の日陰の石近くに八匹の魚が現れました。

slashRows.en: Students added shade and observation position to their log instead of recording temperature alone.
slashRows.jp: 生徒たちは水温だけでなく、日陰と観察位置も記録に加えました。

slashRows.en: Their report said fish sightings changed during the study but did not claim temperature was the only cause.
slashRows.jp: 報告は調査中に魚の目撃数が変わったと述べましたが、水温だけが原因とはしませんでした。

slashRows.en: They suggested measuring at another bridge and at different times before making a stronger ecological conclusion.
slashRows.jp: より強い生態的結論を出す前に、別の橋や異なる時刻でも測ることを提案しました。

slashRows.en: The class learned that a limited observation can reveal a pattern without proving what happens everywhere.
slashRows.jp: クラスは、限られた観察でも傾向は見えるが、どこでも同じだと証明するわけではないと学びました。

passages.title: The Archive Photo Dated by a Store Sign in the Background
sentences: A history club found an undated photograph showing a crowded street near the old station.
The archive card said only that it was probably taken sometime in the 1960s.
In the background, students noticed a shop sign reading 'Aoba Camera, New Building Open.'
A local newspaper index showed that Aoba Camera moved to that building in April 1966.
At first, the club considered labeling the photograph 'April 1966.'
Then a member pointed out that an opening sign might remain for days or weeks after the exact opening date.
The club checked city records and learned that the neighboring pharmacy changed its name in September 1966.
The older pharmacy name was still visible in the photograph.
Together, the clues placed the photograph after the camera shop moved but before the pharmacy changed its name.
The exhibit therefore labeled it 'between April and August 1966' instead of choosing one unsupported day.
A note explained both signs so visitors could see how the date range had been reached.
The club learned that a visual clue can narrow a date strongly without proving more precision than the evidence allows.
passages.fullTranslation: 歴史部は旧駅近くの混んだ通りを写した日付不明の写真を見つけました。資料カードには、一九六〇年代のどこかだろうとだけ書かれていました。背景に「青葉カメラ 新店舗開店」と書かれた看板があることに生徒が気づきました。地域新聞の索引では、青葉カメラがその建物へ移ったのは一九六六年四月でした。部は最初、写真を「一九六六年四月」と表示しようとしました。しかし、開店看板は正確な開店日の後も数日や数週間残ることがあると部員が指摘しました。市の記録を調べると、隣の薬局は一九六六年九月に名前を変えたと分かりました。写真にはまだ古い薬局名が写っていました。二つの手がかりから、写真はカメラ店移転後で薬局改名前だと分かりました。そこで展示は根拠のない一日を選ばず「一九六六年四月から八月の間」としました。来場者が年代幅の根拠を分かるよう、二つの看板を注記しました。部は、視覚的手がかりは年代を大きく絞れても証拠以上の正確さを証明しないと学びました。

slashRows.en: A local newspaper index showed that Aoba Camera moved to that building in April 1966.
slashRows.jp: 地域新聞の索引では、青葉カメラがその建物へ移ったのは一九六六年四月でした。

slashRows.en: At first, the club considered labeling the photograph 'April 1966.'
slashRows.jp: 部は最初、写真を「一九六六年四月」と表示しようとしました。

slashRows.en: Then a member pointed out that an opening sign might remain for days or weeks after the exact opening date.
slashRows.jp: しかし、開店看板は正確な開店日の後も数日や数週間残ることがあると部員が指摘しました。

slashRows.en: The club checked city records and learned that the neighboring pharmacy changed its name in September 1966.
slashRows.jp: 市の記録を調べると、隣の薬局は一九六六年九月に名前を変えたと分かりました。

slashRows.en: The older pharmacy name was still visible in the photograph.

slashRows.en: Together, the clues placed the photograph after the camera shop moved but before the pharmacy changed its name.
slashRows.jp: 二つの手がかりから、写真はカメラ店移転後で薬局改名前だと分かりました。

slashRows.en: The exhibit therefore labeled it 'between April and August 1966' instead of choosing one unsupported day.

slashRows.en: A note explained both signs so visitors could see how the date range had been reached.
slashRows.jp: 来場者が年代幅の根拠を分かるよう、二つの看板を注記しました。

slashRows.en: The club learned that a visual clue can narrow a date strongly without proving more precision than the evidence allows.

passages.title: The Plant-Based Lunch Trial and the Plates Returned Uneaten
sentences: A school offered a plant-based lunch option to one grade for a single Friday.
Students could choose the new meal or the usual chicken meal when they arrived at the cafeteria.
Thirty-six students selected the plant-based meal, but twelve of those trays came back with much of the main dish uneaten.
Some organizers said the trial showed students did not like plant-based food.
A survey after lunch found that several students liked the taste but had taken the option only because the chicken line was long.
Others said the unfamiliar bean portion was larger than they expected.
The committee realized that unfinished food mixed together taste, portion size, and the reason students had selected the meal.
For a second trial, students ordered the option one day earlier and could choose a smaller or regular portion.
Fewer trays returned with large leftovers, although the committee still received mixed comments about the recipe.
The report compared both trials instead of treating one Friday as a final judgment.
It recommended testing more recipes before making a permanent menu change.
The committee learned that participation and leftovers need context before they can explain preference.
passages.fullTranslation: 学校はある学年に一度の金曜日、植物性の昼食を選べるようにしました。生徒は食堂に来たとき新しい食事か通常の鶏肉料理を選べました。三十六人が植物性料理を選びましたが、そのうち十二のトレーは主菜を多く残して戻りました。主催者の一部は、生徒が植物性食品を好まない証拠だと言いました。昼食後の調査では、味は好きでも鶏肉の列が長いから選んだ生徒が何人かいました。ほかには、慣れない豆料理の量が予想より多かったという声もありました。委員会は、食べ残しには味、量、選択理由が混ざっていると気づきました。二回目は前日に注文し、小盛りか普通盛りを選べるようにしました。大量の食べ残しは減りましたが、料理への感想はまださまざまでした。報告は一度の金曜を最終判断にせず、二回の試行を比べました。恒久的にメニューを変える前に、さらに別の料理を試すことを勧めました。委員会は、参加数や食べ残しから好みを説明するには背景情報が必要だと学びました。

slashRows.en: A school offered a plant-based lunch option to one grade for a single Friday.
slashRows.jp: 学校はある学年に一度の金曜日、植物性の昼食を選べるようにしました。

slashRows.en: Students could choose the new meal or the usual chicken meal when they arrived at the cafeteria.
slashRows.jp: 生徒は食堂に来たとき新しい食事か通常の鶏肉料理を選べました。

slashRows.en: Thirty-six students selected the plant-based meal, but twelve of those trays came back with much of the main dish uneaten.
slashRows.jp: 三十六人が植物性料理を選びましたが、そのうち十二のトレーは主菜を多く残して戻りました。

slashRows.en: Some organizers said the trial showed students did not like plant-based food.
slashRows.jp: 主催者の一部は、生徒が植物性食品を好まない証拠だと言いました。

slashRows.en: A survey after lunch found that several students liked the taste but had taken the option only because the chicken line was long.
slashRows.jp: 昼食後の調査では、味は好きでも鶏肉の列が長いから選んだ生徒が何人かいました。

slashRows.en: Others said the unfamiliar bean portion was larger than they expected.
slashRows.jp: ほかには、慣れない豆料理の量が予想より多かったという声もありました。

slashRows.en: The committee realized that unfinished food mixed together taste, portion size, and the reason students had selected the meal.
slashRows.jp: 委員会は、食べ残しには味、量、選択理由が混ざっていると気づきました。

slashRows.en: For a second trial, students ordered the option one day earlier and could choose a smaller or regular portion.
slashRows.jp: 二回目は前日に注文し、小盛りか普通盛りを選べるようにしました。

slashRows.en: Fewer trays returned with large leftovers, although the committee still received mixed comments about the recipe.
slashRows.jp: 大量の食べ残しは減りましたが、料理への感想はまださまざまでした。

slashRows.en: The report compared both trials instead of treating one Friday as a final judgment.
slashRows.jp: 報告は一度の金曜を最終判断にせず、二回の試行を比べました。

slashRows.en: It recommended testing more recipes before making a permanent menu change.
slashRows.jp: 恒久的にメニューを変える前に、さらに別の料理を試すことを勧めました。

slashRows.en: The committee learned that participation and leftovers need context before they can explain preference.
slashRows.jp: 委員会は、参加数や食べ残しから好みを説明するには背景情報が必要だと学びました。

passages.title: The Rooftop Solar Display That Showed Only Sunny Days
sentences: An environmental club made a screen showing how much electricity the school's rooftop solar panels produced.
The first display used four especially sunny days because their graphs were easy to read.
Visitors saw high midday peaks and several assumed the panels produced similar amounts every school day.
A science teacher asked why cloudy and rainy days were missing.
The club realized that choosing only clear examples made the system look more consistent than it really was.
They added one full week containing sunny, cloudy, and rainy weather and labeled each day.
The new graph showed strong production on sunny afternoons and much lower output under thick clouds.
A monthly total remained on the screen so visitors could still see the panels' overall contribution.
The explanation said solar output varied with conditions and did not promise a fixed daily amount.
Students also linked the display to weather records so future viewers could compare changes themselves.
The club kept the sunny-day examples but placed them inside the broader record rather than presenting them alone.
They learned that selecting only attractive data can hide normal variation even when every number shown is true.
passages.fullTranslation: 環境部は学校屋上の太陽光パネルが作る電力量を示す画面を作りました。最初の表示はグラフが読みやすい特に晴れた四日だけを使いました。来場者は正午の高い山を見て、毎日同じ程度発電すると考える人もいました。理科の先生はなぜ曇りや雨の日がないのか尋ねました。部は、分かりやすい例だけを選ぶと実際より安定して見えると気づきました。晴れ、曇り、雨を含む一週間全体を加え、各日の天気を表示しました。新しいグラフでは晴れた午後は高く、厚い雲の下では大きく低下しました。月間合計も残し、全体としてどれだけ役立つかも見られるようにしました。説明には太陽光発電量は条件で変わり、毎日一定ではないと書きました。将来の来場者が自分で比較できるよう気象記録ともつなげました。晴天例は残しましたが、単独でなくより広い記録の中に置きました。部は、示した数字がすべて真実でも都合のよいデータだけ選ぶと通常の変動を隠すと学びました。

passages.title: The Museum Replica Displayed without a Clear Label
sentences: A local museum displayed a bright red helmet beside photographs from a historic fire brigade.
The case label gave the year of the brigade but did not say whether the helmet itself came from that period.
Several visitors assumed they were looking at an original object from the photographs.
A volunteer later checked the collection record and found that the helmet had been made ten years ago for an educational program.
Its shape and color were based on an original helmet kept in storage, but it was a replica.
The museum did not remove it because visitors could safely handle the replica during guided sessions.
Instead, staff changed the label to say 'replica based on the 1952 helmet in our collection.'
A small photograph of the stored original was added beside the explanation.
Visitors could now compare the replica with evidence of the original without confusing the two objects.
The museum also reviewed other hands-on objects for labels that might create the same misunderstanding.
The exhibit became more transparent while keeping the useful teaching object available.
Staff learned that a replica can teach effectively only when visitors are told clearly what it is and what evidence it represents.

passages.title: The Emergency-Drill Rumor Corrected after the Original Notice Was Found
sentences: A message spread among students saying Friday's emergency drill had been canceled.
The message appeared as a screenshot with the teacher's name but no date or full page around it.
Several students planned to move club equipment outside during the time originally reserved for the drill.
One student searched the school's current notice page and found no cancellation.
The teacher then located the original message from the previous month.
It said that an earlier drill had been canceled because of bad weather, not that every future drill was canceled.
The cropped screenshot had removed the date and the sentence naming that earlier day.
The school posted the complete original beside a new message confirming that Friday's drill would happen as planned.
Students who had shared the screenshot were asked to send the correction through the same groups.
Club equipment stayed inside until after the drill, so paths remained clear.

passages.title: The Historical Map with a Place Name That Later Changed
sentences: Students compared an old town map with a modern map while researching a former riverside factory.
The old map marked a place called Sakura Landing beside the river.
The modern map had no Sakura Landing, but it showed Sakura Park several hundred meters upstream.
Some students assumed the park had been built on the exact site of the old landing because the name was similar.
A city record explained that the landing closed in 1958 and that the park received the old district name when it opened in 1974.
The record included coordinates showing that the two sites were not the same.
Students returned to the old map and used a bridge that still existed as a fixed reference point.
That placed the former landing downstream from the modern park, near what is now a parking area.
The project labeled the two sites separately and explained why the shared name could be misleading.
Students also avoided saying the parking area itself had existed when the landing was active.
Their final map used dates and a surviving landmark to connect old and modern geography accurately.
They learned that a place name can move or be reused, so matching names alone does not prove matching locations.
passages.fullTranslation: 生徒たちは川沿いの旧工場を調べるため古い町地図と現在の地図を比べました。古い地図には川のそばに「桜船着場」という場所がありました。現在の地図には船着場はなく、数百メートル上流に桜公園がありました。名前が似ているため、公園が旧船着場と全く同じ場所だと考える生徒もいました。市の記録では船着場は一九五八年閉鎖、公園は一九七四年開園時に旧地区名を受け継いだとありました。記録の位置情報から二つの場所は同じではないと分かりました。生徒は古地図へ戻り、今もある橋を固定した基準点として使いました。その結果、旧船着場は現在の公園より下流、今の駐車場近くにあったと分かりました。調査では二地点を別々に示し、共通名が誤解を招く理由も説明しました。また船着場時代から駐車場があったとは表現しませんでした。最終地図は年代と残る目印を使い、昔と今の地理を正確につなぎました。生徒たちは、地名は移動したり再利用されたりするため、名前の一致だけでは場所の一致を証明しないと学びました。

slashRows.jp: 古い地図には川のそばに「桜船着場」という場所がありました。

slashRows.jp: 現在の地図には船着場はなく、数百メートル上流に桜公園がありました。

slashRows.en: Some students assumed the park had been built on the exact site of the old landing because the name was similar.
slashRows.jp: 名前が似ているため、公園が旧船着場と全く同じ場所だと考える生徒もいました。

slashRows.en: A city record explained that the landing closed in 1958 and that the park received the old district name when it opened in 1974.
slashRows.jp: 市の記録では船着場は一九五八年閉鎖、公園は一九七四年開園時に旧地区名を受け継いだとありました。

slashRows.jp: 記録の位置情報から二つの場所は同じではないと分かりました。

slashRows.en: Students returned to the old map and used a bridge that still existed as a fixed reference point.

passages.title: The Butterfly Survey That Began at the Same Flower Bed Every Day
sentences: A biology club surveyed butterflies in the school garden for ten mornings.
Every day, members began at the bright flower bed beside the south gate and walked the same route.
Their results showed many butterflies near the south gate and very few near the shaded north trees.
The club first planned to report that butterflies strongly preferred the south side of the garden.
Then a student noticed that the survey always reached the north side nearly twenty minutes later.
Butterfly activity could change as the morning warmed, so location and observation time had been linked together.
For another week, the club alternated starting at the north and south ends.
They still saw more butterflies near the sunny flowers, but the difference was smaller than in the first survey.
The report included both weeks and explained the route-order problem in the first method.
The club suggested repeating the study in another season before making a general claim about the whole year.
They learned that a sampling route can bias a result when place and time always change together.
Changing the starting point made their comparison more balanced without erasing the pattern they had actually observed.
passages.fullTranslation: 生物部は十日間の朝、学校菜園でチョウを調査しました。毎日、南門横の明るい花壇から始め、同じ道順を歩きました。結果は南門近くに多く、北の木陰では非常に少ないと示しました。部は最初、チョウが庭の南側を強く好むと報告しようとしました。しかし、調査はいつも北側へ約二十分後に着くと気づきました。朝の気温上昇で活動が変わる可能性があり、場所と観察時刻が結びついていました。次の一週間は北端と南端から交互に始めました。日なたの花近くに多い傾向は残りましたが、最初より差は小さくなりました。報告は両方の週を載せ、最初の方法の道順問題も説明しました。一年全体の一般的結論を出す前に別季節でも繰り返すよう提案しました。部は、場所と時刻が常に一緒に変わると調査経路が結果を偏らせることがあると学びました。開始地点を変えることで、実際に見た傾向を消さず比較をより公平にできました。

slashRows.en: Their results showed many butterflies near the south gate and very few near the shaded north trees.

slashRows.en: The club first planned to report that butterflies strongly preferred the south side of the garden.
slashRows.jp: 部は最初、チョウが庭の南側を強く好むと報告しようとしました。

slashRows.en: Then a student noticed that the survey always reached the north side nearly twenty minutes later.
slashRows.jp: しかし、調査はいつも北側へ約二十分後に着くと気づきました。

slashRows.en: Butterfly activity could change as the morning warmed, so location and observation time had been linked together.
slashRows.jp: 朝の気温上昇で活動が変わる可能性があり、場所と観察時刻が結びついていました。

slashRows.en: For another week, the club alternated starting at the north and south ends.
slashRows.jp: 次の一週間は北端と南端から交互に始めました。

slashRows.en: They still saw more butterflies near the sunny flowers, but the difference was smaller than in the first survey.
slashRows.jp: 日なたの花近くに多い傾向は残りましたが、最初より差は小さくなりました。

slashRows.en: The report included both weeks and explained the route-order problem in the first method.
slashRows.jp: 報告は両方の週を載せ、最初の方法の道順問題も説明しました。

slashRows.en: The club suggested repeating the study in another season before making a general claim about the whole year.
slashRows.jp: 一年全体の一般的結論を出す前に別季節でも繰り返すよう提案しました。

slashRows.en: They learned that a sampling route can bias a result when place and time always change together.
slashRows.jp: 部は、場所と時刻が常に一緒に変わると調査経路が結果を偏らせることがあると学びました。

slashRows.en: Changing the starting point made their comparison more balanced without erasing the pattern they had actually observed.
slashRows.jp: 開始地点を変えることで、実際に見た傾向を消さず比較をより公平にできました。

passages.title: The Vacant Lot Proposed as a Rain Garden
sentences: A vacant lot near a row of houses filled with shallow water after strong rain.
A neighborhood group proposed turning part of it into a rain garden that could temporarily hold storm water.
The first drawing used almost the whole lot for low ground, stones, and water-loving plants.
Several residents liked the flood idea but said children currently used the dry side of the lot for small games.
An older resident also asked who would remove litter and care for plants after the first year.
The group realized that solving drainage by removing every other use could create a different community problem.
They measured where water actually collected after two more storms.
Most water entered from the road side and stayed in the eastern half of the lot.
The western half drained quickly and was the area children used most often.
A landscape volunteer suggested placing the rain garden only in the eastern half and adding a raised path around it.
The revised design kept an open dry area on the west and connected it to the sidewalk.
Native plants were chosen because they could handle both wet periods and several dry days.
The group found monthly maintenance was not enough during the first summer.
A nearby apartment association agreed to rotate weekly checks for litter and blocked drains during that season.
The city approved a one-year trial and asked the group to photograph water levels after major storms.
During the first rainy season, water stayed in the garden instead of spreading across the whole lot twice.
Children continued using the western side after the ground dried, and the raised path kept people out of the wet planting area.
The group still recorded one blocked drain and changed its maintenance checklist rather than calling the trial perfect.
The proposal succeeded because it reduced one flood problem while preserving another valued use and assigning ongoing work.
Residents learned that practical design must fit water, maintenance, and current users.
passages.fullTranslation: 住宅地近くの空き地は強い雨の後、浅い水でいっぱいになりました。地域グループは、その一部を雨水を一時的にためるレインガーデンにする案を出しました。最初の図面では空き地のほぼ全部を低い地面、石、水を好む植物に使いました。洪水対策には賛成する住民も、子どもが今は乾いた側で遊んでいると話しました。高齢の住民は、一年目の後に誰がごみを取り植物を世話するのかも尋ねました。排水を解決するため他の利用をすべてなくすと、別の地域問題を作ると気づきました。さらに二回の嵐の後、水が実際にたまる場所を測りました。水の大部分は道路側から入り、空き地の東半分に残りました。西半分は早く乾き、子どもが最もよく使う場所でした。造園ボランティアは、東半分だけをレインガーデンにし、その周りに高い通路を作る案を出しました。修正版では西側に乾いた広場を残し、歩道とつなげました。在来植物は湿った時期と数日の乾燥の両方に耐えられるため選ばれました。グループは、最初の夏は月一回の管理では足りないと分かりました。近くの集合住宅の会が、その季節はごみと排水口を週ごとに交代で確認することに同意しました。市は一年間の試行を認め、大雨後の水位を写真で記録するよう求めました。最初の雨季には二度、水が空き地全体へ広がらず庭の中にとどまりました。地面が乾いた後も子どもは西側を使い、高い通路によって人が湿った植栽部へ入らずに済みました。排水口の詰まりが一度あり、試行を完璧とせず管理チェック表を修正しました。この案は洪水問題を減らしながら別の大切な利用を残し、継続作業も決めたため成立しました。住民は、実用的な設計には水、管理、現在の利用者を合わせる必要があると学びました。

slashRows.en: A vacant lot near a row of houses filled with shallow water after strong rain.
slashRows.jp: 住宅地近くの空き地は強い雨の後、浅い水でいっぱいになりました。

slashRows.en: A neighborhood group proposed turning part of it into a rain garden that could temporarily hold storm water.
slashRows.jp: 地域グループは、その一部を雨水を一時的にためるレインガーデンにする案を出しました。

slashRows.en: The first drawing used almost the whole lot for low ground, stones, and water-loving plants.
slashRows.jp: 最初の図面では空き地のほぼ全部を低い地面、石、水を好む植物に使いました。

slashRows.en: Several residents liked the flood idea but said children currently used the dry side of the lot for small games.
slashRows.jp: 洪水対策には賛成する住民も、子どもが今は乾いた側で遊んでいると話しました。

slashRows.en: An older resident also asked who would remove litter and care for plants after the first year.
slashRows.jp: 高齢の住民は、一年目の後に誰がごみを取り植物を世話するのかも尋ねました。

slashRows.en: The group realized that solving drainage by removing every other use could create a different community problem.
slashRows.jp: 排水を解決するため他の利用をすべてなくすと、別の地域問題を作ると気づきました。

slashRows.en: They measured where water actually collected after two more storms.
slashRows.jp: さらに二回の嵐の後、水が実際にたまる場所を測りました。

slashRows.en: Most water entered from the road side and stayed in the eastern half of the lot.
slashRows.jp: 水の大部分は道路側から入り、空き地の東半分に残りました。

slashRows.en: The western half drained quickly and was the area children used most often.
slashRows.jp: 西半分は早く乾き、子どもが最もよく使う場所でした。

slashRows.en: A landscape volunteer suggested placing the rain garden only in the eastern half and adding a raised path around it.
slashRows.jp: 造園ボランティアは、東半分だけをレインガーデンにし、その周りに高い通路を作る案を出しました。

slashRows.en: The revised design kept an open dry area on the west and connected it to the sidewalk.
slashRows.jp: 修正版では西側に乾いた広場を残し、歩道とつなげました。

slashRows.en: Native plants were chosen because they could handle both wet periods and several dry days.
slashRows.jp: 在来植物は湿った時期と数日の乾燥の両方に耐えられるため選ばれました。

slashRows.en: The group found monthly maintenance was not enough during the first summer.
slashRows.jp: グループは、最初の夏は月一回の管理では足りないと分かりました。

slashRows.en: A nearby apartment association agreed to rotate weekly checks for litter and blocked drains during that season.
slashRows.jp: 近くの集合住宅の会が、その季節はごみと排水口を週ごとに交代で確認することに同意しました。

slashRows.en: The city approved a one-year trial and asked the group to photograph water levels after major storms.
slashRows.jp: 市は一年間の試行を認め、大雨後の水位を写真で記録するよう求めました。

slashRows.en: During the first rainy season, water stayed in the garden instead of spreading across the whole lot twice.
slashRows.jp: 最初の雨季には二度、水が空き地全体へ広がらず庭の中にとどまりました。

slashRows.en: Children continued using the western side after the ground dried, and the raised path kept people out of the wet planting area.
slashRows.jp: 地面が乾いた後も子どもは西側を使い、高い通路によって人が湿った植栽部へ入らずに済みました。

slashRows.en: The group still recorded one blocked drain and changed its maintenance checklist rather than calling the trial perfect.
slashRows.jp: 排水口の詰まりが一度あり、試行を完璧とせず管理チェック表を修正しました。

slashRows.en: The proposal succeeded because it reduced one flood problem while preserving another valued use and assigning ongoing work.
slashRows.jp: この案は洪水問題を減らしながら別の大切な利用を残し、継続作業も決めたため成立しました。

slashRows.en: Residents learned that practical design must fit water, maintenance, and current users.
slashRows.jp: 住民は、実用的な設計には水、管理、現在の利用者を合わせる必要があると学びました。

passages.title: The Later School Start Trial and the Morning Bus Problem
sentences: A junior high school considered starting first period thirty minutes later for one month.
Students felt tired in early classes, so the health committee tested extra morning time.
The first proposal simply moved every morning activity and the first bell thirty minutes later.
A transport manager pointed out that the school shared buses with an elementary school whose schedule would not change.
If the same buses arrived thirty minutes later, they would still be carrying elementary students on part of the route.
The committee realized that a classroom schedule could not be changed without checking how students reached school.
It surveyed families and found that sixty-two percent used school buses at least three mornings each week.
Some families could drive later, but many said work schedules made that difficult.
The transport company could provide one extra bus, but not enough vehicles to copy the entire route system at a new time.
Instead of canceling the idea, the school designed a smaller trial for students on two routes that the extra bus could cover.
Participation was voluntary, and students on other routes kept the normal start so transport remained available.
Teachers compared attendance, first-period alertness surveys, and late arrivals for the trial group before and during the month.
Most participants reported feeling less sleepy, and late arrivals did not increase.
However, several families disliked having siblings at different schools leave home at more widely separated times.
Teachers warned that the volunteer group might differ from all students.
The report therefore did not claim that a later start was proven best for everyone.
It concluded that sleep-related benefits looked promising but transport capacity and family schedules were major limits.
For the next year, the school asked the bus company to study a route redesign before any larger experiment.
Families could comment on several start-time options instead of only one.
The school learned that start-time changes must fit transport, families, and trial limits.
passages.fullTranslation: 中学校は一か月、一時間目を三十分遅く始めることを検討しました。生徒は朝の授業で疲れを感じており、保健委員会は朝の時間を増やす試行をしました。最初の案は朝のすべての活動と始業ベルを三十分後へ動かすだけでした。交通担当者は、学校が開始時刻を変えない小学校とバスを共有していると指摘しました。同じバスを三十分遅くすると、その時間帯の一部ではまだ小学生を運んでいます。委員会は、登校方法を確認せず授業時刻だけを変えられないと気づきました。家庭調査では六十二パーセントが週三朝以上スクールバスを使っていました。遅く送れる家庭もありましたが、仕事のため難しい家庭も多くありました。交通会社は一台追加できましたが、全路線を別時刻で再現するほど車両はありませんでした。案をやめず、追加バスで対応できる二路線の生徒だけを対象に小規模試行を設計しました。参加は任意で、ほかの路線の生徒は交通を確保するため通常開始を続けました。先生は試行班の出席、一時間目の覚醒度調査、遅刻を試行前と期間中で比べました。多くの参加者は眠気が減ったと答え、遅刻も増えませんでした。一方、兄弟が別の学校へより離れた時刻に出ることを不便に感じる家庭もありました。先生は、希望者集団が全生徒と異なる可能性を指摘しました。そこで報告は、遅い開始が全員に最良と証明されたとはしませんでした。睡眠面の利点は有望だが、交通容量と家庭予定が大きな制約だと結論づけました。翌年に向け、より大きな実験前にバス会社へ路線再設計の検討を依頼しました。家庭は一案だけでなく複数の開始時刻案へ意見を出せました。学校は、開始時刻変更には交通、家庭、試行の限界を合わせる必要があると学びました。

slashRows.en: A junior high school considered starting first period thirty minutes later for one month.
slashRows.jp: 中学校は一か月、一時間目を三十分遅く始めることを検討しました。

slashRows.en: Students felt tired in early classes, so the health committee tested extra morning time.
slashRows.jp: 生徒は朝の授業で疲れを感じており、保健委員会は朝の時間を増やす試行をしました。

slashRows.en: The first proposal simply moved every morning activity and the first bell thirty minutes later.
slashRows.jp: 最初の案は朝のすべての活動と始業ベルを三十分後へ動かすだけでした。

slashRows.en: A transport manager pointed out that the school shared buses with an elementary school whose schedule would not change.
slashRows.jp: 交通担当者は、学校が開始時刻を変えない小学校とバスを共有していると指摘しました。

slashRows.en: If the same buses arrived thirty minutes later, they would still be carrying elementary students on part of the route.
slashRows.jp: 同じバスを三十分遅くすると、その時間帯の一部ではまだ小学生を運んでいます。

slashRows.en: The committee realized that a classroom schedule could not be changed without checking how students reached school.
slashRows.jp: 委員会は、登校方法を確認せず授業時刻だけを変えられないと気づきました。

slashRows.en: It surveyed families and found that sixty-two percent used school buses at least three mornings each week.
slashRows.jp: 家庭調査では六十二パーセントが週三朝以上スクールバスを使っていました。

slashRows.en: Some families could drive later, but many said work schedules made that difficult.
slashRows.jp: 遅く送れる家庭もありましたが、仕事のため難しい家庭も多くありました。

slashRows.en: The transport company could provide one extra bus, but not enough vehicles to copy the entire route system at a new time.
slashRows.jp: 交通会社は一台追加できましたが、全路線を別時刻で再現するほど車両はありませんでした。

slashRows.en: Instead of canceling the idea, the school designed a smaller trial for students on two routes that the extra bus could cover.
slashRows.jp: 案をやめず、追加バスで対応できる二路線の生徒だけを対象に小規模試行を設計しました。

slashRows.en: Participation was voluntary, and students on other routes kept the normal start so transport remained available.
slashRows.jp: 参加は任意で、ほかの路線の生徒は交通を確保するため通常開始を続けました。

slashRows.en: Teachers compared attendance, first-period alertness surveys, and late arrivals for the trial group before and during the month.
slashRows.jp: 先生は試行班の出席、一時間目の覚醒度調査、遅刻を試行前と期間中で比べました。

slashRows.en: Most participants reported feeling less sleepy, and late arrivals did not increase.
slashRows.jp: 多くの参加者は眠気が減ったと答え、遅刻も増えませんでした。

slashRows.en: However, several families disliked having siblings at different schools leave home at more widely separated times.
slashRows.jp: 一方、兄弟が別の学校へより離れた時刻に出ることを不便に感じる家庭もありました。

slashRows.en: Teachers warned that the volunteer group might differ from all students.
slashRows.jp: 先生は、希望者集団が全生徒と異なる可能性を指摘しました。

slashRows.en: The report therefore did not claim that a later start was proven best for everyone.
slashRows.jp: そこで報告は、遅い開始が全員に最良と証明されたとはしませんでした。

slashRows.en: It concluded that sleep-related benefits looked promising but transport capacity and family schedules were major limits.
slashRows.jp: 睡眠面の利点は有望だが、交通容量と家庭予定が大きな制約だと結論づけました。

slashRows.en: For the next year, the school asked the bus company to study a route redesign before any larger experiment.
slashRows.jp: 翌年に向け、より大きな実験前にバス会社へ路線再設計の検討を依頼しました。

slashRows.en: Families could comment on several start-time options instead of only one.
slashRows.jp: 家庭は一案だけでなく複数の開始時刻案へ意見を出せました。

slashRows.en: The school learned that start-time changes must fit transport, families, and trial limits.
slashRows.jp: 学校は、開始時刻変更には交通、家庭、試行の限界を合わせる必要があると学びました。

passages.title: The Reusable Cup Deposit Trial at a Community Event
sentences: A community festival usually used thousands of disposable drink cups during one weekend.
Organizers proposed a reusable cup system with a two-hundred-yen deposit returned when visitors brought cups back.
They expected most visitors to return cups because they would want the money back.
Several food vendors worried that collecting, stacking, and counting used cups would slow already busy serving lines.
The first design placed return boxes at every drink stall.
During a small rehearsal, customers returning cups crossed the same space as people buying drinks, creating confusion.
Organizers realized that a good environmental idea could fail if the return process created too much work at the wrong place.
They moved returns to three separate stations near the main exits and assigned volunteers only to cup collection.
Vendors then needed only to hand out clean cups and collect the deposit with each drink sale.
At the first full festival day, 1,240 cups were issued and 1,083 were returned by closing time.
Missing cups still mattered because replacements used money and resources.
A short visitor survey found that some people had left through a small side gate where no return station was visible.
Others said they had not understood that cups could be returned at any of the three stations rather than only near the original vendor.
For the second day, organizers added return signs at every exit and printed the three-station rule on drink tickets.
The side gate also received a small collection point during the final hour, when many families left at once.
The return rate improved, while vendors reported no longer lines than under the old disposable system.
Volunteers did spend significant time washing and checking cups after the event, so the report included labor as well as waste reduction.
The next festival kept the deposit but budgeted a washing team and improved exit signs from the beginning.
Organizers learned that reuse needs convenient returns, clear information, and realistic staff work.
passages.fullTranslation: 地域祭りでは通常、一週末に何千個もの使い捨てカップを使っていました。主催者は、返却時に二百円が戻るデポジット式の再利用カップを提案しました。来場者は返金を受けたいので大部分が返すだろうと予想しました。食品店は、使用済みカップの回収、積み重ね、数え作業で混雑した販売列がさらに遅くなると心配しました。最初の設計では各飲料店に返却箱を置きました。小さな試行では返却客と購入客が同じ場所を通り、混乱が起きました。主催者は、環境によい案も返却作業が不適切な場所で負担を増やせば失敗すると気づきました。返却を主な出口近くの三つの専用場所へ移し、カップ回収だけを担当するボランティアを置きました。店舗は清潔なカップを渡し、飲料販売時にデポジットを受け取るだけで済みました。本番初日は一二四〇個を貸し出し、閉場までに一〇八三個が返却されました。未返却カップは交換に費用と資源が必要なため問題でした。来場者調査では、返却場所が見えない小さな脇門から帰った人がいると分かりました。元の店の近くだけでなく三か所どこでも返せると理解していない人もいました。二日目は全出口に返却表示を付け、飲料券にも三か所返却の規則を印刷しました。多くの家族が一斉に帰る最後の一時間は脇門にも小さな回収所を置きました。返却率は上がり、店舗は旧使い捨て方式より列が長くならなかったと報告しました。一方、ボランティアは行事後の洗浄と確認にかなり時間を使ったため、報告はごみ削減だけでなく労力も含めました。次回はデポジットを続け、最初から洗浄班の予算と出口表示を用意しました。主催者は、再利用には便利な返却、明確な情報、現実的な人員作業が必要だと学びました。

slashRows.en: A community festival usually used thousands of disposable drink cups during one weekend.
slashRows.jp: 地域祭りでは通常、一週末に何千個もの使い捨てカップを使っていました。

slashRows.en: Organizers proposed a reusable cup system with a two-hundred-yen deposit returned when visitors brought cups back.
slashRows.jp: 主催者は、返却時に二百円が戻るデポジット式の再利用カップを提案しました。

slashRows.en: They expected most visitors to return cups because they would want the money back.
slashRows.jp: 来場者は返金を受けたいので大部分が返すだろうと予想しました。

slashRows.en: Several food vendors worried that collecting, stacking, and counting used cups would slow already busy serving lines.
slashRows.jp: 食品店は、使用済みカップの回収、積み重ね、数え作業で混雑した販売列がさらに遅くなると心配しました。

slashRows.en: The first design placed return boxes at every drink stall.
slashRows.jp: 最初の設計では各飲料店に返却箱を置きました。

slashRows.en: During a small rehearsal, customers returning cups crossed the same space as people buying drinks, creating confusion.
slashRows.jp: 小さな試行では返却客と購入客が同じ場所を通り、混乱が起きました。

slashRows.en: Organizers realized that a good environmental idea could fail if the return process created too much work at the wrong place.
slashRows.jp: 主催者は、環境によい案も返却作業が不適切な場所で負担を増やせば失敗すると気づきました。

slashRows.en: They moved returns to three separate stations near the main exits and assigned volunteers only to cup collection.
slashRows.jp: 返却を主な出口近くの三つの専用場所へ移し、カップ回収だけを担当するボランティアを置きました。

slashRows.en: Vendors then needed only to hand out clean cups and collect the deposit with each drink sale.
slashRows.jp: 店舗は清潔なカップを渡し、飲料販売時にデポジットを受け取るだけで済みました。

slashRows.en: At the first full festival day, 1,240 cups were issued and 1,083 were returned by closing time.
slashRows.jp: 本番初日は一二四〇個を貸し出し、閉場までに一〇八三個が返却されました。

slashRows.en: Missing cups still mattered because replacements used money and resources.
slashRows.jp: 未返却カップは交換に費用と資源が必要なため問題でした。

slashRows.en: A short visitor survey found that some people had left through a small side gate where no return station was visible.
slashRows.jp: 来場者調査では、返却場所が見えない小さな脇門から帰った人がいると分かりました。

slashRows.en: Others said they had not understood that cups could be returned at any of the three stations rather than only near the original vendor.
slashRows.jp: 元の店の近くだけでなく三か所どこでも返せると理解していない人もいました。

slashRows.en: For the second day, organizers added return signs at every exit and printed the three-station rule on drink tickets.
slashRows.jp: 二日目は全出口に返却表示を付け、飲料券にも三か所返却の規則を印刷しました。

slashRows.en: The side gate also received a small collection point during the final hour, when many families left at once.
slashRows.jp: 多くの家族が一斉に帰る最後の一時間は脇門にも小さな回収所を置きました。

slashRows.en: The return rate improved, while vendors reported no longer lines than under the old disposable system.
slashRows.jp: 返却率は上がり、店舗は旧使い捨て方式より列が長くならなかったと報告しました。

slashRows.en: Volunteers did spend significant time washing and checking cups after the event, so the report included labor as well as waste reduction.
slashRows.jp: 一方、ボランティアは行事後の洗浄と確認にかなり時間を使ったため、報告はごみ削減だけでなく労力も含めました。

slashRows.en: The next festival kept the deposit but budgeted a washing team and improved exit signs from the beginning.
slashRows.jp: 次回はデポジットを続け、最初から洗浄班の予算と出口表示を用意しました。

slashRows.en: Organizers learned that reuse needs convenient returns, clear information, and realistic staff work.
slashRows.jp: 主催者は、再利用には便利な返却、明確な情報、現実的な人員作業が必要だと学びました。
